name: HIPAA and Generative AI Tools
blurb: When chatbots can and cannot be used with patient data.
title: HIPAA and Generative AI Tools
answer: Consumer versions of chatbots cannot be used with protected health information, because the vendor will not sign a business associate agreement for them. Enterprise and API offerings can be covered by one, and AI vendors now sell healthcare editions built for that purpose.

reading.body:
Consumer chatbots cannot touch patient data because their vendors will not sign a business associate agreement. Enterprise and API tiers can be covered by one, and vendors now sell healthcare editions built for that purpose.

The dividing line is contractual, not technical. The same underlying model may sit behind both a consumer plan and an enterprise plan, and what separates them is whether the vendor will accept the legal obligations that handling protected health information requires. That makes the business associate agreement the actual gate on clinical use, and it explains why AI vendors have started packaging healthcare-specific offerings rather than leaving hospitals to negotiate access to general products.

For AI in care delivery, this shapes where the compute gets spent. A health system that wants model capability near patient data has to buy it through an enterprise or API channel, which is a narrower and more expensive path than the consumer product most staff already know how to use. The stated risk is not only the ban itself but the workaround: staff denied an approved tool may paste patient data into a consumer one anyway. The recommended control is therefore paired, a prohibition plus a sanctioned alternative.

What this does not cover is the substance of the agreements, what they permit, how long vendors retain data, or how any of it is enforced. It names two vendor developments and no others, so it should not be read as a survey of the market. It also says nothing about the compute or data center footprint behind these tools, and nothing here supports a claim about that.
